info.name: AMS Infotainment API
info.description:
API collection for https://infotainment.ams.com.kh/ — the WordPress backend the Next.js frontend consumes, plus the frontend's own route handlers.

Custom endpoints live in two plugins:
- AMS3E-API (by Sak Ravuth): the wp/v2/web/* article endpoints.
- AMS Frontend API (ours; source at docs/wordpress/ams-frontend-api.php): tv-show-episodes, episode, and /hero-embed.

Common list envelope:
{ "status": "OK", "data": [...], "page": 1, "per_page": 10, "total": "10415", "total_page": 2083 }

Single-object envelope (wp/v2/web/episode):
{ "status": "OK", "data": { ... } }

Note: not every endpoint here is consumed by the frontend — get-article-by-id, find-articles, get-author, the hot-news pair, advertise, secondary-menu and contact-form are documented for completeness. The requests the Next.js app actually issues are marked [frontend] in their descriptions.

Updated 2026-07-13.

item.name: Homepage / Frontend (wp/v2/web — AMS3E-API)
item.description: Custom article/menu/ads endpoints the public frontend uses.

request.description:
[frontend] Main news feed. Returns { status, data[], page, per_page, total, total_page }. Item: { id, title, categories[{id,name,slug}], category (primary slug), slug, post_date (relative Khmer, e.g. '1ម៉ោងមុន'), thumbnail (s3 URL), description }.

Used by src/lib/articles.ts and src/lib/home-data.ts (page_size=9 for the homepage daily/latest grids).

[frontend] Single article detail. Used by src/lib/articles.ts for the article page.

NOTE: returns a RAW object (no {status,data} envelope). Fields: { id, title, thumbnail, categories[{id,name}], publish_date ('YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'), last_updated, description, post_content (Gutenberg HTML), author{id,author_name,profile,description}, seo{title,description} }.
Single article detail by post id (same raw shape as get-article-by-slug).

query.description: Required: category slug (e.g. all-news, entertainment-news, life-style-news)

request.description:
[frontend] Category listing feed. Same list envelope as get-articles. Used by src/lib/articles.ts (page_size=11 for the paginated category page) and src/lib/home-data.ts (slug=life-style-news, page_size=6 for the homepage lifestyle grid).

Note: `total` comes back as a NUMBER here vs a STRING on get-articles — coerce.
Site search.
Author profile.
Latest post in BOTH 'hot-news' and 'entertainment-news' categories within a 2-day window. { status, message, data[] } — often empty.
Same as entertainment hot news but for 'hot-news' + 'life-style-news'. Often empty.

Ads from the wp_ams3e_ads_central table (managed via the Advertisement admin screen). Item: { id, ads_title, ads_location, ads_position, image }. Envelope: { status, message, data[], current_page, per_page, total_items }.
Nav menu for location 'AMS 3E'. Currently 404s because no menu is assigned to that location (Appearance > Menus).
Contact form submission. Fields: full_name, email, question (inserts into wp_ams3e_contact_form + sends a Telegram message).

item.name: AMS Frontend API (custom — docs/wordpress/ams-frontend-api.php)
item.description: Our standalone plugin. Must be installed/active on WordPress. Registers two REST routes (tv-show-episodes, episode) plus the /hero-embed page.

item.name: TV Show Episodes (Obsok / health / any show)

query.description: Required: MasVideos tv_show id. Obsok=14512, One-Minute-for-Health=14570, Daily Feed=84591, The Fact=84589, Reaction=16518, Unlock-the-Life=14288, Tamchet MoMo=69616, Greenbox=14616, Vanayeatra=14450, Studio 11=14564

request.description:
[frontend] Episodes of a TV show, filtered by the MasVideos `_tv_show_id` post meta (not exposed in default REST). Returns { status, data[{ id, title, episode_number ('S1:E44'), permalink, post_thumbnail }], page, per_page, total, total_page }.

Used by src/lib/episodes.ts — backs the program-page carousel and the episode-page season grid.

query.description: Required: episode post id (numeric, > 0). 404s unless the post is a published `episode`.

request.description:
[frontend] Single episode detail — the video source and metadata the default REST route does not expose. Used by src/lib/episode.ts to render the player on every episode page.

Returns a SINGLE-OBJECT envelope: { status: 'OK', data: {...} } — not the list envelope.

data: {
  id, title,
  episode_number  ('S1:E44'),
  run_time        (free text, inconsistently typed: '02:01 នាទី', '02: 15នាទី'),
  release_date    (Unix ts of MIDNIGHT PHNOM PENH TIME — see note below),
  tv_show_id, tv_show_title,
  season_id, season_name ('រដូវកាលទី១', '' when unset),
  post_thumbnail,
  video: { choice, url, attachment, embed }
}

GOTCHA — release_date: Vodi formats this timestamp in UTC and so prints every episode one day early. The plugin returns it RAW; the frontend must format it in Asia/Phnom_Penh. Do not render it as UTC.

[frontend] The wide video banner on the homepage (វនយាត្រា today) — and above the footer on program/episode pages. Used by src/lib/featured-program.ts.

No params. WHICH program is featured, and the artwork behind it, are set in WordPress under Settings → Featured Program (option `ams_afa_featured_program`).

Returns { status: 'OK', data: {...} }, or { status: 'OK', data: null } — NOT a 404 — when nothing is configured or the chosen movie was unpublished. The frontend hides the banner on null.

data: {
  id, slug, title,
  description    (Gutenberg HTML, like core's excerpt.rendered),
  permalink,
  poster         (PORTRAIT, ~346x600 — the movie's featured image),
  cover          (WIDE banner, ~2560x576 — the per-slot artwork),
  release_date   (Unix ts, MIDNIGHT PHNOM PENH — same UTC trap as episodes),
  schedule       (NOT a duration! editors put the broadcast slot in _movie_run_time),
  tv_show_id,
  video: { choice, url, attachment, embed }
}

THREE GOTCHAS, all learned the hard way:
1. `poster` and `cover` are DIFFERENT images — portrait vs ultra-wide. Not interchangeable.
2. `cover` is deliberately NOT the movie's own `_vodi_movie_bg_image`. On vanna-yeatra those are different crops of the same scene — 19925 (2560x576) on the homepage vs 20277 (2560x398) on the movie — so which one fits is a per-slot layout call, mirroring the Vodi `wp:vodi/section-featured-movie` block (which stores movie_id AND bg_image together). Note every variant carries the show's wordmark in the pixels; the frontend prints only a small title label so the logo isn't doubled.
3. `video.embed` GOES STALE — on vanna-yeatra it holds an older Vimeo id than `video.url`. WordPress never shows it (choice is `movie_url`, so Vodi renders `url` via oEmbed). ALWAYS prefer `url`; fall back to `embed` only when `url` is empty.

Renders ONLY the homepage Slider Revolution slider (alias 'homepage-2', id 603) as a standalone HTML page for <iframe> embedding in the frontend. Sends a `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors` header for whitelisted origins. Returns HTML (not JSON).

item.name: MasVideos CPTs (wp/v2)
item.description: Standard REST for the Vodi/MasVideos custom post types. Episodes CANNOT be filtered by show here (the link is private meta) — use tv-show-episodes instead.

request.description: TV Show CPT (programs). e.g. slug=obsok is id 14512.

query.description: trim the heavy default payload (~500KB/item otherwise)

request.description: Episode CPT (all shows, date-ordered). ~1480 total. No show filter in default REST.
Other MasVideos CPTs also exist via standard REST: wp/v2/movie, wp/v2/video, wp/v2/person (swap the path).

query.description: Resolves featured_media into the poster URL

request.description:
[frontend] Title / description / poster for a program page. Used by src/lib/programs.ts (fetchProgramMeta), which holds a hardcoded registry of slug → { postType, postId }. postType is `movie` for most programs; swap the path segment for `tv_show` where the registry says so.

TWO GOTCHAS, both load-bearing:
1. WP core returns ~768KB per movie, nearly all of it Yoast metadata. `_fields` trims it under 8KB.
2. `_links` MUST stay in the `_fields` list or `_embed` yields nothing — the embed resolver walks _links to find the attachment. Drop it and the poster silently comes back empty.

Example id 14516 = 'ពិតអត់' (fact-check).

item.name: Next.js Frontend (own route handlers)
item.description: Endpoints served by the Next.js app itself (src/app/api/**), NOT by WordPress. These run against {{frontend_url}}, not {{base_url}}.

query.description: Required: must equal the REVALIDATE_SECRET env var, else 401.
Cache tag to invalidate. Defaults to 'articles' if omitted.

request.description:
Source: src/app/api/revalidate/route.ts. POST only.

Point a WordPress 'post published/updated' webhook here so fresh content appears immediately instead of waiting out the time-based ISR window (get-articles is cached 300s, article detail 3600s, home feed 120s).

Tags in use across the app:
- articles            (any article list)
- home                (homepage feed)
- article:<slug>      (one article)
- category:<slug>     (one category listing)
- categories          (the category tree)
- episodes            (any episode list)
- episode:<id>        (one episode)
- tv-show:<id>        (one show's episode list)
- program / program:<slug>

Returns { ok: true, revalidated: <tag> } on success, or 401 { ok: false, error: 'invalid secret' }.

Revalidation uses the 'max' profile — stale content is served while it regenerates in the background.
